column1: # FIX-1195 — CAND_ID restore manifest. THIS FILE IS AN AUTHORISATION.
# Three CAND_IDs were ERASED from prod on 2026-09-17 by the nightly promotion.
# promote_candidate_to_elected() merged source_ids as (candidate || elected),
# and jsonb concatenation keeps the RIGHT operand on key conflict, so the
# DELETED elected row's fec_candidate_id overwrote the SURVIVING candidate row's
# own. The code defect is fixed by migration 20260919000000 (on prod
# 2026-09-18 01:47 UTC). This file repairs the data it already destroyed.
# WHY THIS IS URGENT RATHER THAN TIDY. A CAND_ID that no officials row claims is
# re-minted: the cn{yy} stage of the weekly FEC drop creates a fresh candidate
# stub for it. The next drop is the Sunday 2026-09-20 22:44 UTC nightly. Left
# alone, all three return as NEW stubs carrying NEW money and the repair stops
# being a three-row UPDATE.
# HOLDER CENSUS, prod, read 2026-09-18 01:30 UTC — every erased id, every
# surface (live fec_candidate_id / merged_fec_candidate_ids +
# merged_fec_candidate_id / prior_fec_candidate_ids / fec_id):
# The script re-reads this census and REFUSES if any id already has a holder.
# WHAT A ROW AUTHORISES, all three in ONE transaction:
#   1. officials(uuid).source_ids.prior_fec_candidate_ids += restore_id
#   2. for Marshall ONLY, additionally: fec_candidate_id <- S0KS00315, and the
#      House id it currently holds moves into prior_fec_candidate_ids.
#   The UPDATE is keyed by uuid AND asserts expected_current_live_id in its
#   WHERE, so a row that moved since this census was taken matches zero rows and
#   the whole transaction refuses.
# WHY prior_fec_candidate_ids AND NOT merged_fec_candidate_ids, for all three,
# including the two same-chamber cases. Measured from the parsers
# (packages/data/src/pipelines/fec-bulk/claims.ts, index.ts, candidates.ts):
#   array                      | claimed by buildMatchIndex pass 1 | blocks cn re-mint
#   fec_candidate_id           | YES                               | YES
#   prior_fec_candidate_ids    | YES                               | YES
#   merged_fec_candidate_ids   | NO  (authoritativeClaims FILTERS  | NO
#                              |      retired ids out, FIX-955)    |
# So filing an erased id as "retired" leaves it exactly as re-mintable as
# leaving it erased. Only prior_fec_candidate_ids actually restores a claim.
# That array is explicitly NOT role-gated (claims.ts), so a same-chamber entry
# is legitimate — and these are genuinely different seats: H4NC08066/H6NC09200
# are NC-08 and NC-09, H2NJ08232/H2NJ13075 are NJ-08 and NJ-13.
# MARSHALL IS THE ONE THAT ALSO MOVES ITS LIVE ID. 60f87348 is an elected
# Senator holding a HOUSE id (H6KS01179) — the FIX-1187 office-prefix shape. The
# promotion put the Senate stub's money on this row already
# (official_donor_totals $11,374,334, 4,867 FR rows), so restoring S0KS00315 as
# its live id both repairs FIX-1195 and completes FIX-1187 for Marshall. That is
# why Marshall is NOT a row in the set-2 promotion manifest.
# EVIDENCE that each erased id belonged to the row it is restored to: the local
# prod clone, which predates the 2026-09-17 promotion, read 2026-09-18 01:28 UTC:
#     c0af0396  tier=candidate  "Candidate for Representative"  fec_candidate_id=H6NC09200
#     747c96d0  tier=candidate  "Candidate for Representative"  fec_candidate_id=H2NJ13075
#     60f87348  tier=candidate  "Candidate for Senator"         fec_candidate_id=S0KS00315
# and the elected rows the promotion deleted held the ids that survived:
# Each erased id was the promoted row's OWN id. This is a restore, not a guess.
